production.note: US model years for the 306 hp pre-facelift 3.8. First: Hyundai's October 2008 release covers "the All-New 2010 Hyundai Genesis Coupe". Last: the facelifted 2013 car (BK2) introduced the 348 hp direct-injection 3.8 (hyundai-2013-gc-brochure), so the 306 hp car ran through 2012; no opened page states 2012 in so many words. The 2013-2016 car is the separate record hyundai-genesis-coupe-3-8-bk2.

displacementL.note: The brochure states 3.8 liters; no cc figure was on any opened page.

aspiration.note: Inferred: the V6 carries no turbocharger or supercharger (the turbocharged car is the separate 2.0T).

drivetrain.note: "Rear-wheel Drive" standard on all trims; Hyundai calls it "the rear-wheel drive sport coupe" (hyundai-2008-gc-release).

transmission.note: "6-speed Close-ratio Manual Transmission" standard; "ZF 6-speed Electronic Automatic Transmission with Lock-up Torque Converter and Paddle-shift SHIFTRONIC" optional on the 3.8 (the 2008 release names it "ZF 6HP19 6-speed electronic automatic", hyundai-2008-gc-release).

powerHp.note: Quote (2010 brochure spec table): "Horsepower @ rpm (regular fuel) 210 @ 6000 306 @ 6300" (first column the 2.0T, second the 3.8), i.e. 306 hp @ 6,300 rpm on regular fuel. Hyundai's October 2008 release had listed "an estimated 306-hp (regular), 310-hp (premium)" (hyundai-2008-gc-release); the brochure's final published rating on regular fuel is 306 hp.

weightLb.note: Quote (2010 brochure): "Base Curb Weight (lbs.) 3,294 3,389" (second column the 3.8). The brochure does not split the figure by transmission; it is the base 3.8, which comes standard with the 6-speed manual. See discrepancies for the 2008 pre-launch figure.

discrepancies.reason: The October 2008 release's 3,402 lb was pre-launch engineering information (its power figures were labelled estimates); the 2010 brochure prints 3,389 lb.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the brochure's 3,389 lb, the manufacturer's final figure for the 2010 model year.

reviewNotes: End year 2012 is inferred from the 2013 facelift brochure; no opened page states it. Fuel-grade convention also differs between the two Genesis Coupe records: this brochure prints only the regular-fuel 306 hp (Hyundai's 2008 materials said 310 hp on premium), while the BK2 record uses Hyundai's premium-fuel 348 hp headline.
